extracted.intended_audience: FOIA Requesters, Submitters, and NCPC FOIA/records staff
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedures governing Freedom of Information Act (FOIA) requests, responses, fees, exemptions, expedited processing, consultations, referrals, confidential commercial information, appeals, and reading-room materials for the National Capital Planning Commission (NCPC).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Record / Record definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Record or Record means any documentary material which is either created or obtained by a federal agency (Agency) in the transaction of Agency business and under Agency control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include books; papers; maps; charts; plats; plans; architectural drawings; photographs and microfilm; machine readable materials such as magnetic tape, computer disks and electronic data storage devices; electronic records including email messages; and audio-visual material such as still pictures, sound, and video recordings. Generally does not cover records of Agency staff created and maintained primarily for a staff member’s convenience and withheld from distribution to other Agency employees for their official use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Commercial Information (definition and protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential Commercial Information means commercial or financial information obtained by the NCPC from a Submitter that may be protected from disclosure under Exemption 4 of the FOIA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemption 4 protects trade secrets and commercial or financial information obtained from a person which is privileged or confidential. Submitters should mark information in good faith as Confidential Commercial Information. NCPC will follow specific notice, objection, and consideration procedures before disclosing such information (see related entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Controlled Unclassified Information (definition and handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Controlled Unclassified Information means unclassified information that does not meet the standards for National Security Classification under Executive Order 13536, but is pertinent to national interests or important interests of entities outside the federal government and requires protection, special handling, or prescribed limits on exchange or dissemination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When Records are designated Controlled Unclassified Information by another agency, NCPC refers the FOIA Request to that agency; decisions to disclose are based on FOIA exemptions, not on CUI markings alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial Use Request (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Commercial Use Request means a FOIA Request from or on behalf of one who seeks information for a use or purpose that furthers the commercial, trade, or profit interests of the Requester or the person on whose behalf the Request is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial Use Requesters are placed in a separate Requester Category for fee assessment and may be charged Search, Duplication, and Review fees as described in the fees section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct Costs (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct Costs means those expenditures that the NCPC incurs in searching for, duplicating, and reviewing documents to respond to a FOIA Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes, for example, the salary of the employee performing the work (basic rate plus 16% for benefits) and the cost of operating duplicating machinery. Does not include overhead expenses such as costs of space, heating, or lighting where Records are stored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication means the process of making a copy of a document necessary to respond to a FOIA Request in a form that is reasonably usable by a Requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies can be paper copy, audio-visual materials, or machine readable documents (computer disks, electronic data storage devices). Duplication fees apply as specified in the fees section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational Institution (definition and fee treatment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Educational Institution means a school or institution of higher or vocational education operating a program of scholarly research; Requests must be authorized by and made under the auspices of a qualifying institution and records sought to further scholarly research rather than commercial use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational Institutions are a Requester Category for fee determination and may be exempt from certain Search and Duplication fees per the fees section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited Processing (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expedited Processing means giving a FOIA Request priority because a Requester has shown a compelling need for the Records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC will provide expedited processing only when the Request meets specified criteria (see expedited processing criteria entry). A Request for expedited processing may be made initially or later and must include a detailed, certified statement of basis. Decision on expedited requests is made within 10 calendar days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee Waiver (definition and standards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee Waiver means a waiver in whole or in part of fees if a Requester demonstrates certain statutory requirements are satisfied, including that the information is in the public interest and is not requested primarily for commercial purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requesters seeking fee waivers must meet the standards in § 602.15 (referenced) and provide supporting information; fee waivers affect application of fees described in the fees section.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Public Liaison (role)
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA Public Liaison means an NCPC official responsible for assisting in reducing delays, increasing transparency and understanding the status of Requests, and assisting in resolution of disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FOIA Public Liaison assists Requesters in making or correcting Requests and helps resolve time limit disputes; contact information is provided on the NCPC website.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Request (form and submission)
rubrics_metrics.description: FOIA Request or Request means a written Request made by an entity or member of the public for an Agency Record submitted via U.S. mail, electronic-mail (email), facsimile, or other delivery means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To expedite handling, use 'Freedom of Information Act Request' prominently on the envelope or email subject; submit to Chief FOIA Officer at designated NCPC addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading Room Materials and public availability
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall maintain an electronic library at www.ncpc.gov for Reading Room Materials capable of electronic production and an actual public reading room for materials not producible electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reading room available on Workdays 9:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.; appointment requests directed to NCPC’s Information Resources Specialist. Certain types of Records are routinely available without FOIA Request unless exempt (list provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Records Routinely Available Without FOIA
rubrics_metrics.description: The following types of Records shall be available routinely without resort to formal FOIA Request procedures unless exempt: Commission agendas; plans and supporting documentation submitted by applicants; Executive Director’s Recommendations; Commission Memoranda of Action; Transcripts of Commission proceedings; the Comprehensive Plan; Federal Capital Improvements Plan; policies adopted by the Commission; correspondence between the Commission and Congress/other agencies/public; and Frequently Requested Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items should be accessible via the electronic library or reading room unless they fall within FOIA exemptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA Request requirements (content)
rubrics_metrics.description: All FOIA Requests shall be made in writing and must: (1) State that the Request is made pursuant to the FOIA; (2) Describe the Agency Record(s) requested in sufficient detail to enable NCPC to locate them; (3) State a willingness to pay fees or a maximum fee unless seeking a fee waiver or specific Requester Category; (4) State preferred form/format of disclosure if desired; (5) Provide contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sufficient detail includes specific information such as date, title, author, recipient, or time frame. Preferred format will be honored unless it would damage an original or be costly or require new equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification, narrowing, and tolling of response time
rubrics_metrics.description: If a FOIA Request is unclear, overly broad, voluminous, burdensome, or fails to state willingness to pay fees, NCPC shall contact the Requester to define and narrow the Request and obtain fee assurances; the response timeframe is tolled until clarification/payment information is obtained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC will endeavor to assist Requester and will not begin processing until necessary information to clarify the Request and fee issues is obtained; FOIA Public Liaison may assist in this process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief FOIA Officer designation and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall designate a Chief Freedom of Information Act Officer who is authorized to grant or deny any Request for a Record of the NCPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for Records not available in reading rooms are directed to the Chief FOIA Officer; the Officer makes the initial determination within statutory timeframes.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA response timing and determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Freedom of Information Act Officer shall notify the Requester in writing within 20 Workdays of receipt of a perfected Request of the determination to grant or deny the Request, the reasons, and the right to appeal any Adverse Determination to the head of the NCPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In cases involving Unusual Circumstances, the agency may extend the 20 Workday limit by written notice with reasons and expected decision date; extensions generally not more than 10 Workdays unless requester given opportunity to modify or alternative timeframe agreed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial standard and withholding information
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall deny a Request based on a FOIA exemption and withhold information only if NCPC reasonably foresees that disclosure would harm an interest protected by an exemption or if disclosure is prohibited by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a Request is denied, responses must comply with required content (see denial contents entry). NCPC shall release any segregable nonexempt portions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial contents (what must be included when denying)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Request is denied in whole or in part, the Chief FOIA Officer’s written determination shall include, if technically feasible, the precise amount of information withheld, and the exemption under which it is being withheld, unless revealing the exemption would harm an interest protected by the exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC shall release any portion reasonably segregable from exempt portion; written determinations must provide the reasons for denial and notification of appeal rights as described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unusual Circumstances (when to extend time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unusual Circumstances for purposes of extending time limits include: (1) the need to search for and collect Records from establishments separate from Commission offices; (2) the need to search, collect and appropriately examine and review a voluminous amount of separate and distinct Agency Records demanded in a single Request; (3) the need for consultation with another Agency having a substantial interest in the determination of the FOIA Request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensions must be by written notice setting forth reasons and expected dispatch date; extension cannot generally be more than 10 Workdays unless requester offered opportunity to modify or alternative timeframe arranged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-track Processing (use and obligations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multi-track Processing means placing requests in multiple tracks based on the amount of work or time needed to process the request; simple requests in one track, more complex in other tracks, expedited in separate track.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests in each track are processed FIFO. If NCPC uses multi-track processing it shall advise a Requester when a Request is placed in a slower track, inform limits of faster track, and afford requester the opportunity to limit scope to qualify for faster processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing eligibility criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall provide Expedited Processing if the Requester demonstrates the Request involves: (1) circumstances where lack of expedited treatment could pose an imminent threat to life or physical safety; (2) an urgency to inform the public about an actual or alleged federal government activity by a person primarily engaged in disseminating information; (3) the loss of substantial due process rights; or (4) a matter of widespread and exceptional media interest raising questions about government integrity affecting public confidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests relying on the news media category must meet additional requirements (see next entry). Information sought only for historical interest, litigation, or commercial activities will not qualify under the news media criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing requirements for news media Requesters
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify under the news media expedited category, the Requester must establish: (1) they are a full-time Representative of the News Media or primarily engaged in information dissemination; (2) a particular urgency to inform the public about the information beyond the public’s general right to know; (3) the information has value that will be lost if not disseminated quickly (e.g., breaking news).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It need not be the requester's sole occupation; publication contract or past evidence of assignments may indicate basis for expecting publication. Deadlines unrelated to breaking news or information sought for litigation/commercial use will not qualify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited processing decision timeframe
rubrics_metrics.description: Within 10 calendar days of receipt of a Request for expedited processing, the NCPC shall decide whether to grant or deny the Request and notify the Requester in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If granted, request is given priority and processed as fast as practicable in the expedited track; if denied, appeals of that decision shall be acted on expeditiously.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consultations and referrals (when and how NCPC consults or refers)
rubrics_metrics.description: If another agency is better able to determine whether a Record is exempt, NCPC shall either respond after consultation with that agency or refer the responsibility for responding to the originating Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally the originating Agency is presumed best qualified to decide disclosure except for Agency Records submitted to NCPC pursuant to its review authority. Upon referral NCPC shall notify the Requester in writing of the referral, the receiving Agency, the part referred, and a point of contact. Timeframe for response to such requests is based on initial receipt date by NCPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified and Controlled Unclassified Information referral policy
rubrics_metrics.description: For Requests for Records that have been classified or may be appropriate for classification, NCPC shall refer responsibility for responding to the Agency that classified or should consider classifying the Record; for Records designated Controlled Unclassified Information by another Agency, NCPC shall refer to that Agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions to disclose or withhold CUI are made based on statutory FOIA exemptions, not on the CUI marking itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential Commercial Information handling and submitter notice
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall disclose Confidential Commercial Information obtained from a Submitter only in accordance with this section; submitters should designate portions considered protected at submission or reasonably soon after and designations expire after ten years unless justification for longer period provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When NCPC believes requested information is Confidential Commercial Information or it has been designated as such, NCPC will provide prompt written notice to the Submitter describing the requested information or including copies. When notice to many Submitters is required, NCPC may publish/post notice in a place likely to accomplish the intent (newspaper, website, Federal Register).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitter objection and justification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A Submitter given notice shall have a reasonable time to respond and must submit a detailed written statement specifying all grounds for withholding any portion under FOIA exemptions; for Exemption 4 it must show why information is a trade secret or commercial/financial information that is privileged or confidential.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Submitter fails to respond within the specified time, NCPC will consider it no objection and proceed to release. Statements received after NCPC’s disclosure decision will not be considered. Information provided by a Submitter in response may itself be subject to disclosure.

rubrics_metrics.name: NCPC consideration of submitter objections and notice of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall consider a Submitter’s specific grounds for nondisclosure when deciding whether to disclose Confidential Commercial Information. When NCPC decides to disclose over objection it shall give written notice including reasons why objections not sustained, description of information to be disclosed, and a specified disclosure date reasonable subsequent to the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice requirements do not apply if NCPC determines information is exempt, has been lawfully published or made public, disclosure is required by statute/regulation, or the Submitter’s designation appears obviously frivolous (in which case NCPC gives timely written notice of final decision).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notifications related to litigation over Confidential Commercial Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever a Requester files suit to compel disclosure of Confidential Commercial Information, NCPC shall promptly notify the Submitter; NCPC shall also notify the Requester when it provides a Submitter notice and opportunity to object, and shall notify both parties when appropriate about disclosure intentions and lawsuits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC will follow statutory procedures and may provide copies of records to Submitters and Requesters as required by the notice provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals of Adverse Determinations (process and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal of an Adverse Determination must be made in writing to the Chairman of the Commission within 90 Workdays of the date of the notice of an Adverse Determination; words 'Freedom of Information Act Appeal' should appear prominently on the envelope or subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appeals may be submitted by mail, manual delivery, email, or facsimile. The appeal must include a detailed statement of legal/factual basis for objections, contact info, copies of initial request and NCPC response, and for expedited processing or fee waiver adverse determinations a demonstration of compliance with relevant requirements. The Chairman shall respond in writing within 20 Workdays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chairman appeal outcomes and further rights
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Chairman grants the appeal, NCPC shall make available copies of the Requested Records promptly upon receipt of appropriate fee. If denied in whole or part, the denial letter shall state reasons, the FOIA exemptions applied, that the decision is final, notice of right to seek judicial review in federal district court (in certain locales), and notice of alternative dispute resolution options (FOIA Public Liaison or OGIS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NCPC will not act on an appeal if underlying Request becomes subject of FOIA litigation. A party seeking court review must first appeal to NCPC under these procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees: Requester Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: For fee assessment, NCPC categorizes Requesters into three categories: Commercial Use Requesters; Noncommercial Scientific Institutions, Educational Institutions, and News Media Requesters; and all other Requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different fees charged by category; Requesters may seek fee waivers per § 602.15. Fee treatment (e.g., waivers/exemptions from search/duplication) varies by category and circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search fees: who is charged and rate structure
rubrics_metrics.description: NCPC shall not charge Search fees to Educational Institutions, Noncommercial Scientific Institutions, or Representatives of the News Media. NCPC shall charge Search fees to all other Requesters even if no responsive Records are located or are withheld.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Search fees charged by quarter hour based on average GS base salary plus locality plus 16% benefits for Staff Assistant (GS 9–11), Professional Personnel (GS 11–13), and Managerial Staff (GS 14–15). Quarter-hour fees: $9.00 (Staff Assistant), $12.00 (Professional), $18.00 (Managerial). Computer searches may include Direct Costs for creating programs and operator time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication fees: rates and electronic copies
rubrics_metrics.description: Duplication fees are charged to all Requesters subject to limitations: paper photocopy 10 cents/page (single or double sided), 81/2x11 inch color 90 cents/page, up to 11x17 color $1.50/page. For copies produced by computer and placed on electronic data devices or provided as printouts, NCPC charges Direct Costs including operator time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For other forms of duplication, NCPC charges Direct Costs of that duplication. Limits/exemptions may apply per fee limitations section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review fees: applicability and rates
rubrics_metrics.description: Review fees shall be charged only to Requesters who make a Commercial Use Request. Review fees are charged only for the NCPC's initial review to determine whether an exemption applies to a Record or portion thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No charge for Review at administrative appeal level for an exemption already applied, but review on appeal to consider other exemptions may be chargeable. Review fees charged at same rates as Search fees (quarter-hour GS-based rates).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on fees (e.g., failure to meet time limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: If NCPC fails to comply with time limits to respond to a Request, NCPC shall not charge Search fees or, in the case of Educational Institutions, Noncommercial Scientific Institutions, or Representatives of the News Media, duplication fees, except as described in paragraphs (f)(2)–(4) (not included in chunk).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limitation incentivizes timely agency response; other specific fee limitation exceptions and procedures are described elsewhere in the fees section.
